prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a transparent 16-frame RTS soldier animation sheet arranged in EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows, row-major order. Use a large square sheet with ample empty margins per cell, ideally 2048x2048. All 16 frames show the SAME heading specified below; do NOT alternate headings.
Reference image1 is the approved character identity and low-carry running poses; image2 is the approved shouldered, staggered stance and arm action. These are STYLE/IDENTITY/POSE references only; ROTATE THE CHARACTER into the requested heading. Keep the same fixed elevated orthographic camera at about 45 degrees above the ground. This is an upright oblique sprite, not flat overhead. Match its moderately detailed painted little soldier, not chibi or photorealistic.
Materials: shaded saturated MAGENTA helmet, tunic/sleeves and trousers for team-mask extraction. Keep skin natural, hair dark, leather belt/pouches and boots brown, existing wooden rifle stock brown, small barrel/receiver fittings dark steel. No magenta spill on fixed materials. One character, two arms, two boots, one rifle. Preserve right-handed equipment use; DO NOT just mirror the reference. Background genuine transparent alpha, no shadows, no scenery, no labels, no borders, no flashes or smoke.
Frame 1: relaxed standing idle, rifle lowered diagonally across torso, head upright.
Frame 2: alert ready with rifle still low.
Frames 3-8: SIX successive run-cycle poses in the requested heading. Both hands hold rifle securely LOW across the torso below the shoulder, never aimed while running. Alternate forward-foot contact, weight-bearing knee bend, passing/flight, opposite-foot contact, weight-bearing, passing/flight. Legs visibly change, subtle body bob. Maintain consistent pelvis position and ground plane across cells.
Frame 9: settle from running into low ready and begin staggered foot placement.
Frame 10: lift rifle, front foot one comfortable step toward the heading and rear foot behind.
Frame 11: buttplate meets RIGHT shoulder, front knee flexed, weight slightly forward.
Frame 12: fully aimed, cheek on stock, eye aligned along sights; modest staggered standing stance, not a lunge.
Frame 13: small upper-body recoil/compression, both boots stay in the same planted positions.
Frame 14: right hand briefly operates the receiver/bolt, left hand supports fore-end, stock stays at shoulder.
Frame 15: re-aim, operating hand returns, stock and cheek aligned again.
Frame 16: lower rifle, keep staggered planted stance.
Frames 10-16: same planted boots and stable pelvis; only upper body/arms/head change. Every cell is complete full-body at the same anatomical scale, camera and character proportions. Leave enough room for rifle and both boots without clipping.

HEADING CONTRACT: NORTH: directly away from the camera toward screen TOP. All 16 cells are BACK VIEW: back of helmet, jacket back and rear belt visible; face mostly hidden. Running steps move away/up; rifle projects forward away from the back-view body toward upper image with correct foreshortening. Boots remain at the bottom of the upright body. Aimed weapon extends away over the right shoulder toward the TOP, not sideways. Keep the camera fixed, do not turn a west sprite flat in the image plane.

selectedSouth.prompt: Create the south-facing version of this same Rifleman, matching these north, east, and west references. Match their camera, character proportions, stance, detail level, and material colors. Use the same 4-by-4 sixteen-pose layout as the first two references: idle, ready, six running poses, settle, raise, shoulder, aim, recoil, bolt, re-aim, lower. Keep the magenta team materials and natural skin and equipment colors. Every pose should use the same character scale. Transparent background; no shadows, text, or muzzle effects.
selectedSouth.note: User-directed short prompt; no explicit camera-angle or frontal-view instructions.

note: West source sheets are the previously approved carry/run and braced firing references; these original images were reused without regeneration.
